feasibility_reasoning:
The mechanism holds. In node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-server.edge.production.js:2149-2240 (React 19.2.0), pushImg auto-preloads every eager, non-low img that is not inside a picture, keyed by srcSet+"\n"+sizes. With fp=high the preload goes to highImagePreloads, which are flushed before the CSS. The app's own imagePreloadLink element goes through the generic link branch at :1911 (pushLinkImpl(renderState.hoistableChunks)), which does not dedupe. Prod psi/home.html confirms this: link@26362 (1853 B) is a byte-exact copy of React's link@374. OptimizedImage priority gives eager + fp=high with no 'auto,' sizes (atoms/OptimizedImage.tsx:121,125,130). check:bundle, check:chunks, check:entry-purity, check:loader-policy, SSR parity, CLS and SEO are not affected.

Four points weaken it. (1) index.tsx has two coverPreload producers, latest-posts (:156-173) and builder (:236), and head() at :310 cannot tell them apart, so loaderData needs a flag. homeRoute.test.tsx:603-611 asserts the head preload in latest-posts mode. (2) sectionStreaming.tsx:1-5: when the loader deadline is missed, the first fold streams behind a server Suspense gate. React's preload for an img inside that gate then flushes late with the segment, not in head. Today a static hero in such a section still gets the head link (heroImage.ts:89-139 needs no cache for static items), so keeping the Link header at index.tsx:255 is mandatory. (3) The 'audit other routes' step goes beyond the files list. ArchivePosts.tsx:52,75,96 sets priority only when firstCardPriority && idx===0, and head() cannot see that, so dropping the head link on archives can remove the only in-HTML preload. Limit LP-2 to builder docs (index builder branch and $.tsx pages). (4) With React as the single source, whatever is eager gets preloaded and heroImage.ts's caution rules (light/dark :125, logo :130-136, A/B :263) are bypassed. lcpCandidate must keep those rules and also skip hideOn.mobile; today only hideOn.desktop is checked (:204). builderHeroPreload must return null, not fall through, when the candidate's widgetPreload is null.
blocking_issues: head() in routes/index.tsx:310 needs a loaderData flag (builder vs latest-posts) because both modes fill coverPreload. Dropping the head link for latest-posts breaks homeRoute.test.tsx:603-611 and loses the archive-card preload.

The Link header (index.tsx:255, $.tsx:673) must stay. When the hero's section streams behind the Suspense gate (sectionStreaming.tsx:1-5), React's auto-preload is emitted late, not in head, while today the head link covers static heroes in that case.

Do not extend LP-2 to tag/category/blog.index/web-stories/events. Archive priority is conditional (ArchivePosts.tsx:52,75,96 firstCardPriority && idx===0) and invisible to head(), so the head copy is the only safe in-HTML preload there.

lcpCandidate (LP-1) must keep heroImage.ts's exclusions (light/dark pair, logo, abTest) and add hideOn.mobile, because React will preload whatever is eager. builderHeroPreload must return null, not fall through to the next DOM-order widget, when the candidate's preload is null (that would re-create F4 with a now-lazy widget).
effect_reasoning: LP-2's own head change removes one link. I deleted link@26362 from psi/home.html and recompressed: −1853 B raw, −44 B gzip-9. The duplicate srcset sits within 32 KB of link@374, so deflate absorbs it. At 1.6 Mb/s that is 0.2 ms, so 0 in Lantern. The claimed '4 duplicate head links ~7 KB raw / ~1 KB gz' is mostly LP-1's effect: the React duplicates go away only because the cards become lazy. Even combined (keep only the hero preload) it is 7074 B raw / 144 B gz, not ~1 KB. The 'desktop 25vw->480w mis-preload' wastes nothing today. The 480w is also auto-preloaded for the painted eager cards (link@374), and prod-desktop shows 480w and 768w both High from 3405 ms, so the hero is not delayed. After LP-1 alone, an unchanged builderHeroPreload would leave an orphan 25vw head link plus a Link header: +15.8 KB High on desktop, about 13 ms at ~10 Mb/s, so about 0.01 s LCP and < 0.1 pt. On mobile 25vw resolves to 100vw, the same 768w URL, so 0. Lantern sees one network record per URL, initiated by the document, whether the preload comes from the head or the Link header, so moving the source changes no graph edge. A cheaper and more robust alternative: call react-dom preload(href,{as:'image',imageSrcSet,imageSizes,fetchPriority:'high'}) in the route component from loaderData.coverPreload. It shares the imageResources key that pushImg checks (react-dom-server.edge.production.js:2985-2989 vs :2190), so it gives exactly one head preload even when the hero streams late. Simplest of all: keep the head link and only fix the candidate (44 B gz cost).
corrected_estimate: 0 score points on mobile and desktop, today and after LP-1. HTML −1.85 KB raw / −44 B gz for LP-2 alone (−7.1 KB raw / −144 B gz together with LP-1, not ~1 KB gz). It prevents about +0.01 s desktop LCP of orphan-preload regression that LP-1 without LP-2 would introduce. The value is correctness and durability (preload == painted candidate), not score.
better_alternative: Keep a single in-head preload that does not depend on where the img renders. In the route component (SSR shell), call react-dom's preload(desc.href, {as:'image', imageSrcSet, imageSizes, fetchPriority:'high'}) with the lcpCandidate descriptor. React dedupes it with the img's auto-preload through resumableState.imageResources (same srcSet+sizes key), so there is exactly one link in the preamble even if section 0 streams behind the Suspense gate. Keep the Link header. Apply this only to builder docs. Leave posts and archives with their existing head links.
